title: Poetry: words that appeal to the senses (imagery)
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Poems let you see, hear and even smell what is happening. Words that appeal to your five senses create pictures in your mind — this is called imagery. Quick words: imagery means using words to create clear pictures in your mind. strong word means a vivid word that makes you feel or see something clearly.
Imagery uses words that appeal to the senses: sight, sound, smell, taste and touch.
Read these lines: 'The crackling fire glowed warm and bright, / Its smoky scent filled the cold night.'

blocks.question: The word 'crackling' appeals to which sense?
blocks.explain: 'crackling' is a sound you hear, so it appeals to the sense of sound.
blocks.rule: Imagery uses words that appeal to the senses — sight, sound, smell, taste and touch.

practiceItems.prompt: 'glowed bright' appeals to the sense of ___
'smoky scent' appeals to the sense of ___

blocks.content: When you read a poem, notice which sense each strong word is calling to.

blocks.question: 'The juicy, sweet mango dripped down her chin.' Which sense does 'sweet' appeal to?
blocks.explain: 'sweet' is a flavour you taste, so it appeals to the sense of taste.
blocks.rule: Match each sensory word to the sense it appeals to.

practiceItems.prompt: 'soft and fuzzy' appeals to the sense of ___
'loud drums' appeals to the sense of ___
the five senses give a poem strong ___

blocks.question: 'The juicy, sweet mango dripped down her chin.' Which senses does this imagery appeal to?
options: Taste and touch — 'sweet' is taste and 'dripped down her chin' is touch
blocks.explain: Imagery uses words that appeal to the senses so you can almost feel the scene. 'sweet' appeals to taste and 'dripped down her chin' appeals to touch. Sense words make writing vivid.
blocks.rule: Imagery uses sense words (sight, sound, smell, taste, touch) to paint a picture.
blocks.principle: Sense words let the reader experience the scene.
canonical_solution: 'dripped down her chin' appeals to touch
So it appeals to taste and touch

rubric.look_for: explains imagery appeals to the senses

misconceptions.coach: There is no sound word here; look at taste and touch.
